Throwback to that time I had no idea what I was doing and just slammed an entire bag of clay onto the pottery wheel and went for it… I still can’t believe this came out as a finished pot in the end; one that you can spy on my kitchen table in various reels since then.  This doesn’t feel like it was all that long ago but it has been years now. My journey with clay has been up and down since I first shared this, and I don’t know if my journey would have taken me where it did had I never had the urge to see what would happen if I just tried.  This is a throwback video to an oldie but goodie while Courtney and I get on top of our new family of small pots and social media. There’ll be about a week of these repeats. Replying to @naomi when pricing my pieces I consider time spent making/decorating/signing/waxing/glazing/sanding/lustering/firing/invetorying. I have done time studies to help gauge the time I spend on making the pieces. I also consider materials used. I apply gold luster to almost every piece and it’s expensive and requires an additional firing which is also another expense. I also consider experience. I have been working with clay for 14 years now so I consider all of those years of working to this point in my pieces value as well. Pricing is hard! Placing a value on your art is uncomfortable. I’m just happy to be here and I’m doing my best with the knowledge I have gained so far on this journey. I don’t think there is a right answer that will work for everyone, I’m just trying to do what feels right to me! Thank you for reading! 💗💗💗💗 #wheelthrown #ceramics #sliptrailing #potterytiktok #porcelain

This piece of functional art is here to remind you that no matter how gloopy and messy life gets, there is always love and joy bursting through. 🌈💗 I am so excited to finally start sharing the first pieces from my 2026 collection! The first half of this year has been full of learning, experimenting, and pushing my work in new directions. It has also been one of the heaviest seasons of my life. While making this collection, I found myself returning again and again to the same idea: choosing hope. This piece feels like a little celebration of that. A reminder that even when things feel overwhelming, beautiful things can still emerge from the mess. Thankfully, the scary chapter my chosen family has been living through is coming to a very happy ending, and I am sitting in deep gratitude for that. Not everyone gets that outcome, and I don’t take it for granted for a second. So tell me, what makes you stay hopeful when life feels extra gloopy? #ceramicartist #dopaminedecor #glitterinlay #rainbowart #processvideo

This is a process video of how I create my composite filigree pieces. Like this one, I usually use porcelain as my clay body. Combining two separate pieces allows me to work on a larger scale because it would be extremely difficult for me to throw this as a single piece on the wheel. It’s going to have to dry slowly for several days, and then it will have to go through a bisque firing and a glaze firing eventually.  #porcelain #processvideo #ceramics pottery #ceramicsculpture
